+"""Reduction from 3-SAT to Dominating Set.
+
+The source problem is :class:`problems.ThreeSat` and the target is
+``DominatingSet``.  For a formula with ``m`` variables and ``c`` clauses we
+construct a graph with the following gadgets (the classic reduction due to
+Garey & Johnson):
+
+* **Variable gadget** – for each variable ``x_i`` we create two vertices
+  ``T_i`` (representing ``x_i = True``) and ``F_i`` (representing ``x_i =
+  False``) and connect them by an edge.  In any dominating set of size at most
+  ``m + c`` exactly one of the two vertices must be chosen to dominate the
+  edge.
+
+* **Clause gadget** – for each clause we create a triangle of three vertices
+  ``C_{j,0}``, ``C_{j,1}``, ``C_{j,2}``.  The triangle forces the dominating
+  set to contain at least one of its vertices unless a neighbouring literal
+  vertex already dominates it.
+
+* **Literal connections** – each vertex of the clause triangle corresponds to
+  one literal of the clause.  We connect that vertex to the appropriate
+  variable vertex (``T_i`` for a positive literal, ``F_i`` for a negative
+  literal).  Selecting the variable vertex therefore dominates the clause
+  vertex representing a satisfied literal.
+
+With ``n = 2*m + 3*c`` vertices we set ``k = m + c``.  The constructed graph has
+ a dominating set of size at most ``k`` iff the original 3‑SAT formula is
+ satisfiable.
+
+The implementation follows the description above and respects the validation
+rules of the ``DominatingSet`` problem (no duplicate edges, ``u < v`` ordering,
+etc.).

+    if u > v:
